meta.name: Create Kubernetes resources from Slack with Anthropic Claude and safety guardrails

name: AI Kubernetes Create Agent - Manifest Gen, Validation & Approval

parameters.content:
## AI Kubernetes Create Agent - Manifest Gen, Validation & Approval

### How it works

This workflow listens for Kubernetes resource creation requests from Slack or a manual test trigger, then uses an Anthropic-backed AI agent to generate a Kubernetes manifest. It parses and validates the manifest against deterministic guardrails before posting it to Slack for human approval. If approved, it applies the manifest to the Kubernetes API, waits for rollout, verifies health, and either confirms success or rolls the resource back and alerts Slack.

### Setup steps

- Connect Slack credentials for the trigger and notification nodes, and configure the Slack channel or event subscription used for create requests and approvals.
- Connect Anthropic credentials for the manifest generation model used by the AI Agent.
- Configure the Set - Config node with the Kubernetes API base URL, allowed namespaces, requester mapping, and any default request/test values.
- Configure Kubernetes API authentication for the HTTP Request nodes, ensuring the token or credential has only the RBAC permissions required to create, read, and delete the intended resources.
- Review the guardrail validation code to match your cluster policies before enabling production use.
- Configure the Wait approval step so Slack approval responses resume the workflow with the expected approved/rejected payload.

### Customization

Adjust the AI prompt, allowedNamespaces, validation guardrails, rollout grace period, health checks, and rollback behavior to match your Kubernetes resource types and deployment policies.

## Receive creation request

Entry cluster that accepts Kubernetes create requests from Slack or a manual test run, then normalizes shared workflow configuration and request metadata.

## Generate Kubernetes manifest

Uses the AI agent and its Anthropic chat model to turn the request description into a Kubernetes manifest draft.

## Parse and validate manifest

Parses the generated manifest, checks it against deterministic safety guardrails, and branches based on whether validation passed.

## Report validation failure

Notifies Slack when the generated manifest fails guardrail validation, ending the failed path before any approval or cluster action occurs.

## Request human approval

Posts the validated manifest to Slack, waits for a human response, branches on approval status, and sends a rejection notice if declined.

## Apply and check resource

Applies the approved manifest to the Kubernetes API, waits for an initial rollout grace period, and fetches resource status for verification.

## Evaluate rollout health

Evaluates the Kubernetes status response and branches depending on whether the rollout is healthy.

## Confirm successful rollout

Sends a Slack confirmation when the applied resource is verified as healthy.

## Rollback unhealthy rollout

Deletes the resource through the Kubernetes API when rollout health checks fail, then alerts Slack that rollback was triggered.

parameters.text:
=You are a Kubernetes platform engineer. A user asked for the following to be created:

"{{ $json.requestDescription }}"

Generate a complete, production-reasonable Kubernetes manifest as a single JSON object matching the Kubernetes API object shape (apiVersion, kind, metadata, spec, etc. — NOT YAML). Always include a namespace in metadata (pick the most appropriate one implied by the request, defaulting to 'sandbox' if unclear). Always set CPU/memory requests AND limits on every container. Never set privileged: true, never use hostNetwork, never use hostPath volumes. Use reasonable defaults for anything unspecified (e.g. a small resource footprint, a public well-known image if none is given).

Return ONLY a JSON object (no markdown fences, no commentary) with keys: manifest (the Kubernetes object as a nested JSON object), resourceKind (string, e.g. 'Deployment'), namespace (string), explanation (2-3 plain-English sentences describing what this creates and why you made the choices you did).
=:x: Kubernetes create request for *{{ $json.resourceKind }}* in `{{ $json.namespace }}` was rejected. No changes were made.
=:white_check_mark: *{{ $json.resourceKind }}* `{{ $json.manifest.metadata.name }}` created in `{{ $json.namespace }}` and is healthy ({{ $json.readyReplicas }}/{{ $json.desiredReplicas }} ready).

=:rotating_light: *{{ $json.resourceKind }}* `{{ $json.manifest.metadata.name }}` in `{{ $json.namespace }}` failed its health check ({{ $json.readyReplicas }}/{{ $json.desiredReplicas }} ready) and has been automatically rolled back (deleted).
